target.title: fix(node-pairing): enforce cross-device ownership on node.pair.approve
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a non-admin operator device could approve node capability grants belonging to a device it does not own. On the gateway, `node.pair.approve` authorized purely against the caller's session scopes and never checked whether the caller device owns the node it is approving. A paired operator device holding only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` (a real, supported non-admin grant, no `operator.admin`) could call `node.pair.approve` with another device's pending `requestId` and immediately arm that node's declared commands. Because `mcp.tools.call.v1` maps to `[operator.pairing, operator.write]` (not the admin-gated `system.run` tier), it gets armed without the separate admin allow-commands step, and `node.invoke` then only requires `operator.write`, so the same non-admin caller can invoke it against a node it does not own without the real admin ever reviewing that device's grant.

This is the node-surface sibling of gaps already closed elsewhere: `device.pair.approve` (`src/gateway/server-methods/devices.ts`) and `node.pair.remove` (`src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`) both already deny non-admin cross-device management. `node.pair.approve` had neither check. `git log -p` shows it was never wired in (an omission, not a regression).

## Why This Change Was Made

`node.pair.approve` now resolves the pending request's owning node id before approval and denies when `deniesCrossDeviceManagement` holds, mirroring the exact guard already used by `node.pair.remove` and `device.pair.approve`. A read-only `getPendingNodePairing(requestId)` accessor (sibling of `getPendingDevicePairing`) supplies the owning node id. The guard only bites device-token self-service sessions (`callerDeviceId` set, non-admin) approving a different device; shared-auth operators (`callerDeviceId` null, the CLI/Control UI/admin approval path) and admin callers are unaffected, so the existing non-admin, scope-gated node-surface approval flow keeps working. The node role itself was already admin-approved at device-pairing time and surface danger stays scope-gated, so no role-management-requires-admin check is added here.

## User Impact

Operators can no longer arm node commands on a device they do not own using a non-admin paired-device session. Legitimate approvals are unchanged: shared-auth and admin operators approve node surfaces exactly as before, and a device-token session may still approve its own node surface. A denied cross-device attempt returns `node pairing approval denied` and emits a `device.pairing.approval_denied` security event.

## Evidence

Regression tests added to `src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts` drive the real gateway WS server end to end:
- `denies a non-admin device-token session approving another device's node surface` (fails on pristine main, passes with patch)
- `allows a shared-auth operator session to approve another device's node surface` (proves the legit path is preserved)

Verification (run from a deps-enabled worktree against identical copies of the changed files):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts` -> `Tests 28 passed (28)`
- `oxlint` on the three changed files -> clean
- `oxfmt --check` on the three changed files -> clean
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` -> clean; core-test lane clean for the changed files (only unrelated `ui/@codemirror` module-resolution noise from the local run environment)

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a non-admin device-token operator session (`operator.pairing` + `operator.write`, no `operator.admin`) can approve another device's pending node surface via `node.pair.approve` over the gateway WebSocket and arm its declared commands.
Real environment tested: a running gateway booted through the production `startGatewayServer` boot on a real `127.0.0.1` loopback port, driven over real `ws` WebSocket connections that complete the real connect handshake and send `node.pair.approve` as an over-the-wire JSON-RPC request. The victim node is paired through the real `requestDevicePairing`/`approveDevicePairing` reducers, the attacker session is a real device token from `issueOperatorToken`, and armed commands are read back from the real `listNodePairing()` store. Driven with only the two changed files reverted to pristine `main` `176647aa845763639f7c0b982e91b3c68730163f` versus this PR head `d1a1031ed2e8b137791732ca3229af04415b3da8`; the rest of the tree is identical between runs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: boot the gateway, pair a victim node device and create its pending node surface declaring `mcp.tools.call.v1`, open an attacker device-token WebSocket scoped to exactly `operator.pairing` + `operator.write`, send `node.pair.approve` with the victim's `requestId`, then open a shared-auth operator WebSocket and approve an equivalent surface; record each raw response frame and the victim's armed commands.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 176647aa845763639f7c0b982e91b3c68730163f)
gateway listening ws://127.0.0.1:41000 pid=3226765

[attacker] non-admin device-token session (operator.pairing, operator.write)
[attacker] wire frame: {"type":"res","id":"8dde5e7b-b0ef-4359-94ff-bcf80b6f7ea8","ok":true,"payload":{"requestId":"29d800ab-3b6e-4268-8892-82955623005e","node":{"nodeId":"node-cross-device-victim","commands":["mcp.tools.call.v1"],"createdAtMs":1783834599139,"approvedAtMs":1783834599139}}}
[attacker] approve.ok=true error=null
[attacker] victim armed commands=["mcp.tools.call.v1"]

[shared-auth] operator session (callerDeviceId null)
[shared-auth] approve.ok=true
[shared-auth] node armed commands=["mcp.tools.call.v1"]

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head d1a1031ed2e8b137791732ca3229af04415b3da8)
gateway listening ws://127.0.0.1:39000 pid=3226658

[attacker] non-admin device-token session (operator.pairing, operator.write)
[attacker] wire frame: {"type":"res","id":"03d05711-7792-46ea-bead-5f6178747ea3","ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"node pairing approval denied"}}
[attacker] approve.ok=false error="node pairing approval denied"
[attacker] victim armed commands=null

[shared-auth] operator session (callerDeviceId null)
[shared-auth] approve.ok=true
[shared-auth] node armed commands=["mcp.tools.call.v1"]
```
Observed result after fix: on pristine main the non-admin cross-device caller receives an `ok:true` frame over the socket and arms `mcp.tools.call.v1` on a device it does not own; with this patch the identical caller receives `ok:false` `node pairing approval denied` and arms nothing, while the shared-auth operator still approves the identical surface and arms `mcp.tools.call.v1`.
What was not tested: no live iOS/macOS/Android node client or real APNs wake, and the gateway was booted through the production `startGatewayServer` boot in a single process rather than the packaged CLI daemon; no full build was run.
